plugins.name: claude-architect
plugins.description: A recursive multi-agent orchestration framework for Claude Code: an orchestrator that decomposes work into epics/specs/implementations, runs each in an isolated git worktree, and drives a review + architecture-audit + merge pipeline before every squash-merge. Ships nine role-pinned subagents, an /architect skill that classifies and routes every change request, and the methodology that ties them together.

plugins.name: claude-boundaries
plugins.description: Makes an architecture's layer, container and contract boundaries mechanically enforceable — and makes every coding agent inherit them. A declared container map drives a zero-dependency import checker wired into hooks: a violating edit is fed straight back to the agent, and no agent may finish a turn with a violating tree. Nine rules cover direction, layer skipping, declared edges, public surface, purity, escaping relative imports, third-party imports, package-manifest agreement and type-only edges.

plugins.name: godot-lsp
plugins.description: GDScript code intelligence for Claude Code. Godot ships a real language server but only listens on TCP, while Claude Code runs every LSP server over stdio — its `transport: "socket"` option is accepted and then ignored, so the two never meet. This bridges them with a dependency-free 55-line pipe, giving hover, go-to-definition, find-references, symbols and diagnostics on .gd files from the engine's own analyser, built-in class documentation included. Requires the Godot editor to be open, since the language server lives in the editor rather than the engine.

plugins.name: rig-anything
plugins.description: Rigs and animates an arbitrary Blender mesh, including shapes no template covers. The work is split by what each side is actually good at: deterministic Python measures the geometry, and vision classifies it from rendered silhouettes, because geometry alone cannot tell a dog from a table and counting ground contacts cannot tell front from back. A skeleton is then fitted from a template where one fits and built from a discovered Reeb graph where none does, bound with bone-heat weights, and given a looping gait for any number of legs - or a travelling lateral wave for a body with none. Export writes glTF along with the playback speed the clip's own stride implies, then reads the file back to check it. Every measurement is defended: bone axes are probed per bone because an elbow and a knee bend opposite ways, and a rig whose pose evaluation has gone stale errors instead of returning a confident table of zeros.
